_comment: The arc, as data. Beat conditions are engine expressions (api/engine.py), so a beat completes because the run or the corpus says so -- never because the interface set a flag on its own. Keep every 'say' and every card body under ~180 characters: the dialogue panel wraps at 46 columns by 4 lines. The text path has no em-dash glyph; write --.
prologue: Everything alive here carries light. A person, a hound, a thing in the long grass -- each holds a little, and spends it.
Knowledge is the same. A page somebody read and vouched for burns steadily. A page nobody opened goes dark, and something moves into the dark.
Lately the light has been leaving. A lamp at a time, a page at a time, until a land has gone quiet and no one recalls it was otherwise.
Somebody decided to stop it. If light will not stay in a lamp, she reasoned, fix it into something that cannot put it down. She began with a moth.
Now the hares burn crimson and the herons burn gold, and every one is running down. What burns out does not die. It crosses.
You are a probe: one quantum given a body, sent in to find where the light is going. You will be spent doing it. That is what a probe is for.
Out in the grass is a hound made of the same light, who does not spend what he carries. Nobody ever marked his line. Find him.

rigour.name: The Order of Rigour
rigour.creed: Light that misleads is worse than dark.
rigour.wants: every label accounted for, every derivation checked, every source named
rigour.critical: an unstated assumption, a wrong unit, a claim with nothing behind it
rigour.belief: A lamp hung over a pit kills more people than the dark did. Unmark what was marked. Check what was claimed.
rigour.on_marking: Vesper never wrote down which dye went into which animal. Two hundred lines, no ledger. That is the crime -- not the marking, the silence.

clarity.name: The Order of Clarity
clarity.creed: Light nobody can reach is light nobody has.
clarity.wants: a stranger at the door and through it in five minutes
clarity.critical: a term used before it is defined, a step nobody explains
clarity.belief: The Fading is not a loss of light. It is a loss of doors. The knowledge still burns; nobody can get to it any more.
clarity.on_marking: Every keeper can see a marked hare and not one in twenty can read what is in it. Teach them, and the Marking stops being magic.

discovery.name: The Order of Discovery
discovery.creed: What is unwritten is not therefore unimportant.
discovery.wants: the gaps found, the unlinked mapped, the silence named
discovery.critical: an orphan, a dead link, a hole in the tree
discovery.belief: The worst dark was never lit at all. Counting the lamps you already have is how a world agrees to stop looking.
discovery.on_marking: Nobody asked the obvious question. The light is not destroyed -- it goes somewhere, and something down there is receiving it.

beats.headline: Wake. Someone is standing over you.
beats.body: Grass, sky, and a stranger's voice. Probes arrive the way light does -- suddenly, and without luggage. The keeper beside you has been waiting.

beats.headline: Something glows faintly in the grass.
beats.body: A hound of light, run down to an ember, curled where the road bends. He does not spend what he carries, so if he is dim he has been alone a long time.
beats.goal: Find the dim hound and speak to him.

beats.headline: Something in the grass is the wrong colour.
beats.body: A hare, burning gold. Not lit -- burning, the way a lamp burns when somebody stopped watching it. It cannot stop running.

beats.headline: The label can come off.
beats.body: Wear it down until it lets go, then take it. The animal is free and the dye is yours to give to somebody who agreed to carry it.
beats.goal: Take a label off a marked animal.

beats.headline: Lit ground still exists. Learn what keeps it burning.
beats.body: A lit page is one a person read and vouched for, and its keeper stands at the door. There are far fewer keepers than doors.
beats.goal: Stand in a settlement where at least one house is lit.

beats.headline: Something walked this ground ahead of you.
beats.body: Some houses are half-lit -- a cold, borrowed glow with nobody at the door. Something read what was there, and no person confirmed a word of it.
beats.goal: Find half-lit ground -- a house burning with nobody keeping it.

beats.headline: The Wardens will not let you past untrained.
beats.body: Five of them, one to a crossing. What shining costs, what colour is for, what the glass decides, what is underneath, and where any of it came from.

beats.headline: Three orders will each tell you what the Marking is.
beats.body: Rigour says she wrote nothing down. Clarity says nobody was taught to read a label. Discovery says nobody asked where the light goes.
beats.goal: Find an emissary and pledge to an order.

beats.headline: Your order has work for you.
beats.body: A pledge is words until ground changes hands. Your order's lands hold rooms nobody has faced. Clear them, and the doctrine stops being an opinion.
beats.goal: Clear 3 rooms in your order's lands.

beats.headline: There is a cave in every cliff, and they all go down.
beats.body: A label driven all the way down does not stop existing. It crosses, into the state underneath this one. Ovid has been, and would rather you saw it.
beats.goal: Go down through a cave mouth.

beats.headline: Everything she ever marked is down here.
beats.body: The same country with the light taken out, and standing in it the shapes of animals you have seen alive and in colour. None of them attacks you.
beats.goal: Walk the dark manifold and find what is at the middle of it.

beats.headline: The tower in the ash was built, not left.
beats.body: Vesper is at the top of it, and has been expecting somebody a long time. She will show you the ledger before she shows you anything else.
beats.goal: Reach the tower at the heart of the dark, and hear her out.

beats.headline: The dark has given ground. Come and see.
beats.body: Not everywhere, and not for good. But where you worked the lamps hold, and a land that watched light leave for years has watched it come back.

lanternwright: So the Wellspring sent a probe. They always send something that cannot survive the errand.
Look at the ledger before you look at me. Six lands. Four hundred years of the Fading, stopped, by one woman with a needle.
You have been going about unbinding my work. Every label you took off, I put on something that was going dark.
Where do you imagine that light went when you took it? Into your pocket. We are the same, probe. I did it at scale.

replies.rigour: You never wrote down which dye went into which animal. That is not saving light. That is hiding it.
replies.clarity: Nobody you saved can read what is in them. When you go, six lit lands go dark in a week.
replies.discovery: You never asked where it went. It came down here, it is standing behind you, and it has waited a long time to be counted.
replies.none: I have no argument yet. I have a pocket of labels I took off animals that did not consent, and so do you.

rigour: The ledger is open. Every marked line she made is written down, with the dye, the body and the date. Merel walks the shelves without a taper.
Rigour does not celebrate. But the books close with more light in them than they opened with, and every lamp stands over checked ground.
clarity: Doors stand open along the Pilgrim Road, and in each of them somebody is being taught to read a label. Five minutes, and a stranger knows.
The light was there all along. What you built were doors, and the Fading walks past a door it cannot close.
discovery: The map has fewer blank places, and one is not blank at all: the country underneath is drawn, named, and counted.
What you found was always there. Now it is findable, and that is the difference between a world and a rumour of one.
